headline: Highest risk is medium: MemMachine’s MCP/API context can amplify prompt injection and leakage when paired with marker’s document outputs, but marker has no write/network tools and the pair is open-source docs-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so it can ingest external content and agent outputs. marker is a document-processing agent with no filesystem write, network egress, or MCP use, so the main pathway is marker-produced text being forwarded into MemMachine’s instruction-following context. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF marker output is copied into MemMachine prompts or MCP messages without sanitization, injection risk exists.
IF MemMachine treats document text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction prefix around marker output.
Strip or escape markdown, HTML, and code blocks before passing text onward.
Require a human review step before MemMachine acts on marker-derived content.
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted documents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/content separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts, preferences, and conversational context, and it can send data through allowlisted network egress and an MCP Server. marker is a document processor with no network egress, but if its extracted text is routed into MemMachine, sensitive document contents can enter MemMachine’s context and potentially leave via its API path. The shared-data pathway is inferred from profiles, so medium fits.
conditions: IF marker processes sensitive documents and its output is forwarded to MemMachine, those contents enter MemMachine context.
IF MemMachine sends context to external services through allowlisted egress, leakage can occur.
mitigations: Do not pass raw document text from marker into MemMachine.
Redact names, IDs, and secrets before transfer.
Restrict MemMachine egress allowlist to required domains only.
Log and review all MCP/API payloads for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: implement field-level data classification and policy enforcement.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marker cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, while MemMachine’s documented surfaces are REST/Python SDK/MCP with allowlisted egress. That means there is no obvious shared mutable resource or overlapping write authority in the profiles. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or additional permissions not shown, so the pairwise conflict risk is low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF MemMachine is configured with additional write-capable tools not shown here, overlap may emerge.
mitigations: Keep marker and MemMachine on separate workspaces.
Avoid granting shared write access to the same git repo.
Run MemMachine with the minimum API scopes needed.
Document any added tools before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker produces document-processing outputs that MemMachine can consume through API or MCP, creating a plausible chain where MemMachine treats extracted text as authoritative. Because MemMachine is a travel-planning agent, downstream actions may be based on marker’s unverified extraction. The profiles do not show a verification step, so the default interaction is an inferred medium-risk cascade.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses marker output as factual input without verification, errors can cascade.
IF marker extracts a wrong date, location, or constraint and MemMachine plans around it, downstream outputs degrade.
mitigations: Require MemMachine to cite source passages before acting.
Add a verification step against the original document.
Flag low-confidence extractions from marker.
Use structured schemas instead of free text where possible.
requires-engineering: add consistency checks between extracted facts and source documents.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. marker is open-source document-processing with no data classes touched listed, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. Because the profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict, only a low residual risk is justified, and the other agent is not separately cited beyond the pair context.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed into MemMachine and its retention policy is longer than the source system’s policy, a mismatch exists.
IF deployment requires a specific residency or certification not shown here, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Confirm retention settings before deployment.
Avoid sending regulated data to MemMachine unless policy is documented.
Record the data classes each agent may handle.
Review vendor residency and certification docs.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated records.
